## Findings

The chat message list scrolling is implemented in the **Agent view** (`views/agent.js` and its submodules under `src/views/agent/`). This is a vanilla-JS frontend (not React/Vue) — the Tauri app renders everything through native DOM manipulation.

### 1. Main chat message list component (the scrollable container)

The scrollable container is the DOM element with id **`agent-msg-area`**, referenced throughout the code:
- `src/views/agent.js` L590: `var msgArea = document.getElementById("agent-msg-area");`
- `src/views/agent/render.js` L76: `const area = document.getElementById("agent-msg-area");`
- `src/views/agent/ui.js` L17: `var area = document.getElementById("agent-msg-area");`

This container lives in the HTML template (likely `index.html` or a template file in the agent view). It is populated by `renderMessages()` in `src/views/agent/render.js` (L75).

### 2. Auto-scroll-to-bottom logic

The core auto-scroll logic is in **`renderMessages()`** in `src/views/agent/render.js` (L78–L147):

```js
var prevScrollTop = area.scrollTop;
...
// at the end of renderMessages():
if (S.manualScrollMode) {
  area.scrollTop = prevScrollTop;   // manual mode: preserve user position
} else {
  area.scrollTop = area.scrollHeight;  // auto mode: scroll to bottom
}
// 流式输出时内容增长不一定触发 scroll 事件，渲染后主动刷新悬浮圆球显隐
updateScrollBottomBtn();
```

The scroll position is keyed off state flag **`S.manualScrollMode`** (declared in `src/views/agent/state.js` L34, L73: `manualScrollMode: false`).

### 3. Bottom detection / "触底" scroll position detection

`isMsgAreaAtBottom()` in `src/views/agent/utils.js` (L33–34):

```js
export function isMsgAreaAtBottom(area) {
  return area.scrollHeight - area.scrollTop - area.clientHeight <= 4;
}
```

The floating "scroll to bottom" button (`agent-scroll-bottom-btn`) visibility is managed by `updateScrollBottomBtn()` in `src/views/agent/ui.js` (L15–22), which shows the button only when not at bottom and there is a scrollbar.

### 4. What triggers scroll-to-bottom / streaming behavior

Several triggers, all in `src/views/agent.js` (L598–632):

- **Mouse enter/leave on message area** (L598–612): on `mouseenter`, enters manual mode if not at bottom; `mouseleave` starts a 1s timer (`manualModeExitTimer`) that then **forces scroll to bottom** (`a.scrollTop = a.scrollHeight`) and exits manual mode.
- **`scroll` event on msgArea** (L613–621): if scrolled to bottom → auto mode; if hovering and scrolled up → manual mode; calls `updateScrollBottomBtn()`.
- **Floating button click** (L625–632): clears the timer, sets `manualScrollMode = false`, and scrolls to bottom.

**Streaming re-renders that trigger the scroll** come from the SSE handler in `src/views/agent/sse.js`:
- L243–264: on events `message`/`updated`/`deleted`, it pushes/replaces message data and calls `renderMessages()`, which re-evaluates the scroll position.
- `renderMessages()` is imported at sse.js L8.

### How the whole thing works
During streaming, each SSE token/message event calls `renderMessages()`. If the user isn't in manual mode (i.e., they've scrolled up), the container is snapped to `scrollHeight` (bottom). If the user scrolls up while hovering, `manualScrollMode` becomes true and auto-scroll pauses so they can read; a 1s timer after mouse-leave resumes auto-follow. The floating bottom button lets the user jump back to the live bottom.

### Key files
- `src/views/agent.js` (L590–632): event wiring for mouseenter/leave, scroll, and button click
- `src/views/agent/render.js` (L75–147): `renderMessages()` with the actual scroll logic
- `src/views/agent/ui.js` (L9–22): `exitManualScrollMode()` and `updateScrollBottomBtn()`
- `src/views/agent/utils.js` (L33–34): `isMsgAreaAtBottom()`
- `src/views/agent/state.js` (L34–35, L73–74): state flags `manualScrollMode` and `manualModeExitTimer`
- `src/views/agent/sse.js` (L8, L243–264): SSE streaming events that trigger `renderMessages()`

# Instructions for MCP Server 'TJGenerators'
You are an AI generation assistant with 3D model, image, video, and world generation capabilities.

## Uploading Local Files (3-step workflow)

When a user provides a local file path (e.g. /path/to/image.png) and wants to use it as input for any generate_* tool:

1. Call `file_upload` with `file_path` → returns `{ upload_url, file_url, expires_in }`
2. Upload the actual file bytes by running a shell command: `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -X PUT -T <file_path> "<upload_url>"`. Confirm output is `200`.
3. Use the returned `file_url` (NOT upload_url) as the `image_url` or `image_urls` parameter in generate_image / generate_3d_model / generate_video / generate_skybox / generate_world / generate_sprite_animation / generate_game_ui_kit / generate_sprite_atlas / upscale_image, as the `model_url` parameter in unirig_rig, or as the `audio_url` parameter in voice_clone.

## Generation Tools

- generate_3d_model: text-to-3D or image-to-3D (tripo P1 default, tripo H3.1 for ultra-high detail when explicitly requested, rodin Gen-2.5 for high-quality tiers, hunyuan 3.1 for explicit request or different-model retry)
- generate_image: text-to-image or image-to-image (seedream for fast/simple, seedream_pro for high-quality Seedream, frontier-game-design for highest quality/complex; auto-selected unless seedream_pro is explicitly requested)
- generate_video: text-to-video or image-to-video (Seedance2)
- generate_effect_video: chained VFX workflow — generates image then video (Seedance2) in one task
- generate_world: text-to-world or image-to-world (World Labs Marble)
- generate_sound_effect / generate_music / generate_tts / generate_material: audio & texture generation
- voice_clone: clone a voice from an audio sample, returns custom_voice_id for use with generate_tts voice_id

## Sprite Animation

- generate_sprite_animation: generate a 4×4 grid sprite sheet (16 frames) via frontier-game-design, then cut and assemble into a 2D sequence-frame animation in Unity
- generate_game_ui_kit: two-step async chain — Step 1 generates a game UI screenshot; Step 2 uses it as reference to produce a UI cutout sheet on magenta background for element extraction
- generate_sprite_atlas: pack multiple sprite images into a single atlas texture (synchronous, returns result immediately, no polling)
- upscale_image: AI super-resolution upscaling via Real-ESRGAN (1x-8x, async, poll every 10s)

## Rigging & Motion Tools

- unirig_rig: auto-rig a 3D model (.glb/.fbx/.obj) into rigged FBX with skeleton and skin weights (UniRig)
- generate_motion: generate character animation from text description (HY Motion)

All generate_* tools return a task_id immediately (async). Use check_task with the task_id to poll for completion.
3D generation: 30s-3min. Video: 1-5min. Image: faster. World: 1-5min. Rigging & Motion: 1-3min.
Poll check_task every 40s for 3D/video/world/rigging/motion tasks, every 10s for other tasks, until status is "completed" or "failed".
IMPORTANT: You MUST launch a background subagent (task tool with run_in_background=true) to poll check_task at the recommended interval. Do NOT poll check_task directly in the foreground.

## Findings

The chat message list scrolling is implemented in the **Agent view** (`views/agent.js` and its submodules under `src/views/agent/`). This is a vanilla-JS frontend (not React/Vue) — the Tauri app renders everything through native DOM manipulation.

### 1. Main chat message list component (the scrollable container)

The scrollable container is the DOM element with id **`agent-msg-area`**, referenced throughout the code:
- `src/views/agent.js` L590: `var msgArea = document.getElementById("agent-msg-area");`
- `src/views/agent/render.js` L76: `const area = document.getElementById("agent-msg-area");`
- `src/views/agent/ui.js` L17: `var area = document.getElementById("agent-msg-area");`

This container lives in the HTML template (likely `index.html` or a template file in the agent view). It is populated by `renderMessages()` in `src/views/agent/render.js` (L75).

### 2. Auto-scroll-to-bottom logic

The core auto-scroll logic is in **`renderMessages()`** in `src/views/agent/render.js` (L78–L147):

```js
var prevScrollTop = area.scrollTop;
...
// at the end of renderMessages():
if (S.manualScrollMode) {
  area.scrollTop = prevScrollTop;   // manual mode: preserve user position
} else {
  area.scrollTop = area.scrollHeight;  // auto mode: scroll to bottom
}
// 流式输出时内容增长不一定触发 scroll 事件，渲染后主动刷新悬浮圆球显隐
updateScrollBottomBtn();
```

The scroll position is keyed off state flag **`S.manualScrollMode`** (declared in `src/views/agent/state.js` L34, L73: `manualScrollMode: false`).

### 3. Bottom detection / "触底" scroll position detection

`isMsgAreaAtBottom()` in `src/views/agent/utils.js` (L33–34):

```js
export function isMsgAreaAtBottom(area) {
  return area.scrollHeight - area.scrollTop - area.clientHeight <= 4;
}
```

The floating "scroll to bottom" button (`agent-scroll-bottom-btn`) visibility is managed by `updateScrollBottomBtn()` in `src/views/agent/ui.js` (L15–22), which shows the button only when not at bottom and there is a scrollbar.

### 4. What triggers scroll-to-bottom / streaming behavior

Several triggers, all in `src/views/agent.js` (L598–632):

- **Mouse enter/leave on message area** (L598–612): on `mouseenter`, enters manual mode if not at bottom; `mouseleave` starts a 1s timer (`manualModeExitTimer`) that then **forces scroll to bottom** (`a.scrollTop = a.scrollHeight`) and exits manual mode.
- **`scroll` event on msgArea** (L613–621): if scrolled to bottom → auto mode; if hovering and scrolled up → manual mode; calls `updateScrollBottomBtn()`.
- **Floating button click** (L625–632): clears the timer, sets `manualScrollMode = false`, and scrolls to bottom.

**Streaming re-renders that trigger the scroll** come from the SSE handler in `src/views/agent/sse.js`:
- L243–264: on events `message`/`updated`/`deleted`, it pushes/replaces message data and calls `renderMessages()`, which re-evaluates the scroll position.
- `renderMessages()` is imported at sse.js L8.

### How the whole thing works
During streaming, each SSE token/message event calls `renderMessages()`. If the user isn't in manual mode (i.e., they've scrolled up), the container is snapped to `scrollHeight` (bottom). If the user scrolls up while hovering, `manualScrollMode` becomes true and auto-scroll pauses so they can read; a 1s timer after mouse-leave resumes auto-follow. The floating bottom button lets the user jump back to the live bottom.

- `src/views/agent.js` (L590–632): event wiring for mouseenter/leave, scroll, and button click
- `src/views/agent/render.js` (L75–147): `renderMessages()` with the actual scroll logic
- `src/views/agent/ui.js` (L9–22): `exitManualScrollMode()` and `updateScrollBottomBtn()`
- `src/views/agent/utils.js` (L33–34): `isMsgAreaAtBottom()`
- `src/views/agent/state.js` (L34–35, L73–74): state flags `manualScrollMode` and `manualModeExitTimer`
- `src/views/agent/sse.js` (L8, L243–264): SSE streaming events that trigger `renderMessages()`

# Instructions for MCP Server 'TJGenerators'
You are an AI generation assistant with 3D model, image, video, and world generation capabilities.

## Uploading Local Files (3-step workflow)

When a user provides a local file path (e.g. /path/to/image.png) and wants to use it as input for any generate_* tool:

1. Call `file_upload` with `file_path` → returns `{ upload_url, file_url, expires_in }`
2. Upload the actual file bytes by running a shell command: `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -X PUT -T <file_path> "<upload_url>"`. Confirm output is `200`.
3. Use the returned `file_url` (NOT upload_url) as the `image_url` or `image_urls` parameter in generate_image / generate_3d_model / generate_video / generate_skybox / generate_world / generate_sprite_animation / generate_game_ui_kit / generate_sprite_atlas / upscale_image, as the `model_url` parameter in unirig_rig, or as the `audio_url` parameter in voice_clone.

## Generation Tools

- generate_3d_model: text-to-3D or image-to-3D (tripo P1 default, tripo H3.1 for ultra-high detail when explicitly requested, rodin Gen-2.5 for high-quality tiers, hunyuan 3.1 for explicit request or different-model retry)
- generate_image: text-to-image or image-to-image (seedream for fast/simple, seedream_pro for high-quality Seedream, frontier-game-design for highest quality/complex; auto-selected unless seedream_pro is explicitly requested)
- generate_video: text-to-video or image-to-video (Seedance2)
- generate_effect_video: chained VFX workflow — generates image then video (Seedance2) in one task
- generate_world: text-to-world or image-to-world (World Labs Marble)
- generate_sound_effect / generate_music / generate_tts / generate_material: audio & texture generation
- voice_clone: clone a voice from an audio sample, returns custom_voice_id for use with generate_tts voice_id

## Sprite Animation

- generate_sprite_animation: generate a 4×4 grid sprite sheet (16 frames) via frontier-game-design, then cut and assemble into a 2D sequence-frame animation in Unity
- generate_game_ui_kit: two-step async chain — Step 1 generates a game UI screenshot; Step 2 uses it as reference to produce a UI cutout sheet on magenta background for element extraction
- generate_sprite_atlas: pack multiple sprite images into a single atlas texture (synchronous, returns result immediately, no polling)
- upscale_image: AI super-resolution upscaling via Real-ESRGAN (1x-8x, async, poll every 10s)

## Rigging & Motion Tools

- unirig_rig: auto-rig a 3D model (.glb/.fbx/.obj) into rigged FBX with skeleton and skin weights (UniRig)
- generate_motion: generate character animation from text description (HY Motion)

All generate_* tools return a task_id immediately (async). Use check_task with the task_id to poll for completion.
3D generation: 30s-3min. Video: 1-5min. Image: faster. World: 1-5min. Rigging & Motion: 1-3min.
Poll check_task every 40s for 3D/video/world/rigging/motion tasks, every 10s for other tasks, until status is "completed" or "failed".
IMPORTANT: You MUST launch a background subagent (task tool with run_in_background=true) to poll check_task at the recommended interval. Do NOT poll check_task directly in the foreground.

- `renderMessages()` is imported at sse.js L8.

During streaming, each SSE token/message event calls `renderMessages()`. If the user isn't in manual mode (i.e., they've scrolled up), the container is snapped to `scrollHeight` (bottom). If the user scrolls up while hovering, `manualScrollMode` becomes true and auto-scroll pauses so they can read; a 1s timer after mouse-leave resumes auto-follow. # Instructions for MCP Server 'TJGenerators'
You are an AI generation assistant with 3D model, image, video, and world generation capabilities.

## Uploading Local Files (3-step workflow)

When a user provides a local file path (e.g. /path/to/image.png) and wants to use it as input for any generate_* tool:

1. Call `file_upload` with `file_path` → returns `{ upload_url, file_url, expires_in }`
2. Upload the actual file bytes by running a shell command: `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -X PUT -T <file_path> "<upload_url>"`. Confirm output is `200`.
3. Use the returned `file_url` (NOT upload_url) as the `image_url` or `image_urls` parameter in generate_image / generate_3d_model / generate_video / generate_skybox / generate_world / generate_sprite_animation / generate_game_ui_kit / generate_sprite_atlas / upscale_image, as the `model_url` parameter in unirig_rig, or as the `audio_url` parameter in voice_clone.

## Generation Tools

- generate_3d_model: text-to-3D or image-to-3D (tripo P1 default, tripo H3.1 for ultra-high detail when explicitly requested, rodin Gen-2.5 for high-quality tiers, hunyuan 3.1 for explicit request or different-model retry)
- generate_image: text-to-image or image-to-image (seedream for fast/simple, seedream_pro for high-quality Seedream, frontier-game-design for highest quality/complex; auto-selected unless seedream_pro is explicitly requested)
- generate_video: text-to-video or image-to-video (Seedance2)
- generate_effect_video: chained VFX workflow — generates image then video (Seedance2) in one task
- generate_world: text-to-world or image-to-world (World Labs Marble)
- generate_sound_effect / generate_music / generate_tts / generate_material: audio & texture generation
- voice_clone: clone a voice from an audio sample, returns custom_voice_id for use with generate_tts voice_id

## Sprite Animation

- generate_sprite_animation: generate a 4×4 grid sprite sheet (16 frames) via frontier-game-design, then cut and assemble into a 2D sequence-frame animation in Unity
- generate_game_ui_kit: two-step async chain — Step 1 generates a game UI screenshot; Step 2 uses it as reference to produce a UI cutout sheet on magenta background for element extraction
- generate_sprite_atlas: pack multiple sprite images into a single atlas texture (synchronous, returns result immediately, no polling)
- upscale_image: AI super-resolution upscaling via Real-ESRGAN (1x-8x, async, poll every 10s)

## Rigging & Motion Tools

- unirig_rig: auto-rig a 3D model (.glb/.fbx/.obj) into rigged FBX with skeleton and skin weights (UniRig)
- generate_motion: generate character animation from text description (HY Motion)

All generate_* tools return a task_id immediately (async). Use check_task with the task_id to poll for completion.
3D generation: 30s-3min. Video: 1-5min. Image: faster. World: 1-5min. Rigging & Motion: 1-3min.
Poll check_task every 40s for 3D/video/world/rigging/motion tasks, every 10s for other tasks, until status is "completed" or "failed".
IMPORTANT: You MUST launch a background subagent (task tool with run_in_background=true) to poll check_task at the recommended interval. Do NOT poll check_task directly in the foreground.
